title: Integration testing between services and the ordering problem

videos.script: A test that passes alone and fails in the suite is one of the most common defects in test code. {{alone}} This lesson is about where it comes from, and about tests that cross more than one service. You start with the test runner already inside Node. No framework, nothing to install. {{node-test}} Then a test that goes through two programs. boxoffice takes an order, the payments stub takes the charge, and the test checks both sides. {{two}} Then the ordering problem. Two tests share one show with four seats. Each passes on its own. Together, one of them fails. {{four-seats}} You will see why, and fix it by giving each test file a server of its own. {{fix}} Then a report that lags half a second behind the orders. A test that reads it at once fails. A test that sleeps is slow, and still fails some days. {{lag}} You will write a small helper that asks again until a deadline, and fails with the reason. {{eventually}} Last, a script that starts the services in order, waits until each one answers, and runs the suite. {{script}} By the end, your tests give the same answer in any order, on any machine.
